c01_phone_standard.csv.desc: Baseline 一生足迹 export (11 columns): city walk, foreground ~3 s, background 20-30 s stretches, ~50% accuracy = 0, rest 5-65 m (median 15 m). Accuracy column -> phone. Gaps counted by the timeGap rule on the exact written coordinates.

c02_reordered_cols.csv.desc: Columns reordered and capitalised (Latitude,Longitude,Altitude,Accuracy,dataTime,...) in Santiago: every data line starts with '-' (negative latitude). 3 rows have an empty dataTime -> kept as untimed points (lat/lon valid). Accuracy column -> phone.

c03_no_accuracy.csv.desc: 一生足迹-style CSV without the accuracy column: no creator, no accuracy -> profile decided by sampling regularity; ~3 s foreground + 20-30 s background is not 'steady' (median dt 3 > 2) -> phone.

c04_quoted_emptylines.csv.desc: Every field double-quoted (header too), an extra trailing "address" column containing a comma, and 8 junk lines (empty, blanks only, commas only) plus trailing empty lines. All 255 data rows must load; accuracy -> phone.

c05_loctype_variants.csv.desc: Standard columns, but locType cycles 0/1/2/3/5/6/-1, isBackForeground 0/1/2/empty/true/false, stepType 0/1/2/-1/empty, heading and speed -1, distance sometimes empty. None of these columns is read; every row must load. Accuracy -> phone.

c06_all_acc_zero.csv.desc: Standard 一生足迹 columns but accuracy = 0 (unknown) on every row: the accuracy median ignores zeros -> nil, so the profile falls back to sampling regularity -> phone (median dt 3 s, 20-30 s background steps).

c07_crlf_bom.csv.desc: UTF-8 BOM + CRLF line endings (Excel re-save). Header must still be recognised (BOM and \r trimmed), altitude field ends in \r. Accuracy -> phone.

c08_headerless.csv.desc: No header line: numeric first character -> fixed 一生足迹 layout (0=time, 2=lon, 3=lat, 5=accuracy, 10=altitude). Accuracy -> phone.

c09_millis_minimal.csv.desc: Minimal 4 columns (no altitude) with millisecond epoch times (1.7e12 > 4e10 -> divided by 1000). Accuracy -> phone.

c10_iso_time.csv.desc: dataTime as ISO 8601 strings instead of epoch: every 3rd row local '+08:00', others 'Z' with or without '.000'. Same instants as a normal export; accuracy -> phone.

c11_semicolon.csv.desc: European-locale export: ';' delimiter and decimal commas. Header has no commas -> not sniffed as CSV -> .noPoints is the expected outcome (loading with decimal-comma truncation would be wrong data). Must not crash.

c12_header_only.csv.desc: Header line only, no data rows: CSV layout found, 0 rows -> .noPoints.

c13_bad_rows.csv.desc: 400 good rows plus 12 junk rows: lat 95, lon 200, NaN, null, empty lat/lon, an error message, a '#' comment, a truncated row, swapped lat/lon (lat 126.5), a repeated header (concatenated exports), a row with empty dataTime and one with dataTime 'abc'. Junk with invalid coordinates must be dropped; the last two have valid coordinates and may be kept as untimed points or skipped (points 400-402, timed 400).

c14_random_numeric.csv.desc: Chaos: 2000 headerless numeric rows (fixed 一生足迹 layout) - times clustered in 50 min with many per-second collisions plus 0, -1, 1e308, NaN, inf, 4e10+1 (ms branch), 99999999999 (> 1e11 -> NaN); coordinates in a 10 km box, a 60-point exact-repeat pool, global random, poles/antimeridian, out-of-range; short rows, inserted columns, garbage first fields. Purely a no-crash / no-hang / invariant test: accept or reject, any counts.

c15_single_row.csv.desc: Header + exactly one data row: 1 point; accuracy median needs >= 20 samples -> nil, no timed steps -> profile unknown. All detectors empty.

g01_empty_0byte.gpx.desc: 0-byte file: GPXParser.parse throws .empty (n <= 8). Must not crash.

g02_tiny_8byte.gpx.desc: 8-byte '<gpx/>' + CRLF: exactly at the n > 8 guard -> .empty. Must not crash.

g03_header_only.gpx.desc: Valid GPX with metadata (incl. a metadata <time>) but no trk/rte/wpt: parser throws .noPoints.

g04_no_trkpt.gpx.desc: trk with two empty trkseg (one self-closing), no trkpt: .noPoints expected.

g05_one_point.gpx.desc: Single trkpt (eTrex creator -> deviceLogger by creator). timedCount 1: detect/replay/jitter guards (n<2, n<3, n<8) must return empty; trips 0.

g06_two_points.gpx.desc: Two fixes 30 s / ~600 m apart (72 km/h): the minimal timeGap -> exactly 1 gap. Profile from 1 step is meaningless (any).

g07_no_time.gpx.desc: 240 trkpt with ele but no <time>: timedCount 0, all detectors return empty. Creator matches no rule and there are no timed steps -> unknown.

g08_half_time.gpx.desc: 300 trkpt, odd ones without <time> (interleaved): load must stable-sort the 150 timed points first (2 s steps, cycling). Creator contains 'android' -> phone.

g09_out_of_order.gpx.desc: 600 s car drive at 1 Hz written as 12 shuffled 50-point blocks (one block reversed). After the load-time sort it is one clean drive: 0 gaps/jitter; any missed sort would show up as 5-30 km jumps. Times are unique, so the unstable vDSP sort is irrelevant.

g10_dup_timestamps_50.gpx.desc: Walk at 1 Hz; fixes 150-199 all carry the same timestamp while the position keeps advancing (70 m), then the clock resumes (+50 s). dt=0 steps (infinite speed) must not crash speed/profile code; per-second jitter sample = median of 50 points, ~35 m steps: no jump, no gap (steps < 150 m).

g11_dup_points.gpx.desc: 300 cycling fixes, each written twice (every 15th three times) with identical lat/lon/time - a double import. dt=0 duplicates are not replays (replay needs >= 10 s), no gaps, no jitter. Creator 'android' -> phone.

g12_missing_ele.gpx.desc: 500 s cycling at 1 Hz with no <ele> at all (ele = NaN everywhere). Wahoo creator -> deviceLogger. Clean track: 0 gaps / replays / jitter.

g13_multi_trk_seg.gpx.desc: [2026-10-29 调整] Two tracks in reverse chronological order, 2 + 3 explicit hard source segments. Each segment is internally continuous; the 120 s / ~1.5 km transition is a source boundary. Therefore 0 gaps and 5 trips. 调整理由：旧扁平期待gap1/trips4会跨源段连接；独立逐段旧算法与生成器真值确认五段各自连续，改为gap0/trips5。

g14_waypoints_only.gpx.desc: 30 <wpt> POIs only (10 self-closing, entities and CJK in <name>), 6 with <time> 3-15 h apart: the parser keeps wpt as points; timed 6, spacing > 3600 s -> 0 gaps; jitter needs >= 8 timed points -> 0. Garmin creator -> deviceLogger.

g15_route_only.gpx.desc: Route only: 150 <rtept> (no time, one line each). Parser keeps rtept as points; timed 0 -> nothing to detect; BRouter creator -> unknown.

g16_mixed_wpt_rte_trk.gpx.desc: 5 untimed <wpt> + 40 untimed self-closing <rtept> before a 400-point timed <trk>: timed points come after NaN times, so the load sort must move them to [0, 400). 445 points, 400 timed, clean ride.

g17_dateline.gpx.desc: Ferry at ~9 m/s, 1 Hz, lat -16.75, lon 179.875 -> -179.9: crosses the antimeridian at t=1716040703. Haversine steps are <= 12 m everywhere, so truth is 0 gaps and 0 jitter. jitter_free guards the crossing: detectJitter's planar frame uses an unwrapped lon2-lon1, which turns the 8 m crossing step into a ~38,000 km westward step (counted as a reversal); any jitter here is that bug.

g18_near_pole.gpx.desc: Snowmobile 8 m/s, 1 Hz, from lat 89.9 (lon 20) over the pole (closest fix 43 m) to lat ~89.9 on lon -160: longitude sweeps 180 deg in ~1 min and passes the antimeridian ~100 m from the pole at t=1716060605. Real steps are <= 12 m, so truth is 0 gaps / 0 jitter. Any jitter is a detector artefact (unwrapped lon2-lon1 in the planar lon*cos(lat) frame: the 8 m step 179.75 -> -178.90 becomes dx = -680 m). Mercator clamp at 85.05 must not crash.

g19_southern_western.gpx.desc: 900 s car drive at 1 Hz in Buenos Aires: negative lat AND lon everywhere. Clean track: 0 gaps / replays / jitter.

g20_equator_greenwich.gpx.desc: Ship at 8 m/s crossing the equator and the prime meridian; the fix nearest (0,0) (4 m off) is written as exactly lat="0.0000000" lon="0.0000000" - must stay a normal point (not treated as 'no fix'). 0 gaps / jitter.

g21_invalid_coords.gpx.desc: 300 valid cycling fixes (some written as 5.25e+01 exponent, '+13.4', leading blanks, newline/tab between attributes) plus 13 invalid trkpt: lat 95, lon 200, lat -90.0000001, lon -180.0000001, NaN, nan, empty, missing lat, 1e999, abc, --5, upper-case LAT/LON. All invalid ones must be dropped. One extra trkpt uses single-quoted attributes (valid XML; this parser only matches lat="); points 300-301 either way.

g22_crlf.gpx.desc: 300 s cycling, 1 Hz, every line ends in CRLF (Windows export). Clean: 0 gaps / jitter.

g23_bom.gpx.desc: UTF-8 BOM before <?xml ...?>, 300 s walk at 1 Hz. The BOM must not break format sniffing (first line has '<' -> GPX) nor creator lookup (Suunto -> deviceLogger).

g24_garmin_ext_ns.gpx.desc: Garmin Connect style: XML comments (before root, between laps, after root), 5 namespaces, metadata/track <extensions>, TrackPointExtension (hr/cad/atemp) inside every trkpt, lon-before-lat attributes split over lines, 5 fixes with the 9.999999562023526e+24 'no elevation' sentinel. A comment contains a commented-out untimed <trkpt> at fix 0's position: a byte-scanning parser counts it, so points 600-601; timed is 600 either way. 0 gaps / jitter.

g25_ns_prefixed.gpx.desc: Namespace-qualified GPX (<gpx:trkpt>, prefix bound to the GPX 1.1 namespace) - valid XML but the byte scanner matches only unprefixed '<trkpt '. Rejection (.noPoints) is acceptable; a namespace-aware parser would load 200 points, 0 gaps.

g26_fractional_offsets.gpx.desc: 900 s cycling, fixes at whole seconds +-0.2 s written with millisecond fractions; first 300 as local +02:00, next 300 as Z, last 300 as -03:30 - one continuous UTC timeline. Wrong offset handling would create 2 h / 3.5 h holes and reorderings: trips 1 and 0 gaps only if offsets are applied.

g27_time_1970.gpx.desc: 600 s walk at Greenwich from 1969-12-31T23:58:00Z to 1970-01-01T00:07:59Z: unix times -120..479 including exactly 0. Negative and zero times are valid ISO 8601 and must not be treated as 'no time': timed 600, trips 1, 0 gaps.

g28_time_2100.gpx.desc: 1800 s ride from 2100-02-28T23:45:00Z across midnight into 2100-03-01 (2100 is NOT a leap year; times ~4.1e9). A wrong leap rule would open a 24 h hole -> trips 2. Expect trips 1, 0 gaps, timed 1800.

g29_minified_oneline.gpx.desc: Whole document on one line, no trailing newline: attribute order varies, tab between attributes, <time> before <ele> on half the fixes, whitespace inside <time> on every 5th fix (XML-valid for xs:dateTime). 400 s ride, 0 gaps / jitter.

g30_truncated.gpx.desc: Recording cut off mid-file (battery): 500 complete fixes, the 501st ends inside '<time>2024-05-19' with no closing tags. Keeping the partial fix untimed or dropping it are both fine (points 500-501, timed 500). No crash, 0 gaps.

g31_bad_time_formats.gpx.desc: 240 s walk; 9 fixes carry unparsable times ('2024/05/19 ...', bare epoch digits, empty <time></time>) -> untimed; one carries '2024-13-45T25:61:61Z', which this parser does not range-check and turns into a finite time ~9 months later (2025-02-15) -> it sorts last, separated by > 3600 s: no gap, a lone 1-point tail is not a trip. timed 230-231 (231 if the month-13 time is accepted).

g32_fit_binary.gpx.desc: A Garmin .FIT binary (14-byte header + 4 KB random records) saved with a .gpx extension. Expect .noPoints (or any rejection); must not crash or hang.

g33_html_error.gpx.desc: An HTML 404 page saved as .gpx (failed download); contains <tr>/<td>/<title> that share prefixes with <trkpt>/<time>. Expect .noPoints; must not crash.

g34_gpx10_speed_course.gpx.desc: GPX 1.0 (GPSBabel, ISO-8859-1 declaration): top-level <time> and <bounds/>, per-point <time> before <ele>, plus <course>/<speed>/<sat>/<hdop>/<fix>. 300 s ride; 0 gaps / jitter. No creator signal; steady 1 Hz sampling -> deviceLogger by the regularity rule.

g35_boundary_coords.gpx.desc: 40 timed fixes hopping between coordinates exactly ON the valid limits (lat +-90, lon +-180, -0.0, 0, 89.9999999/179.9999999) at 1 s and 30 s steps; (0,180)/(0,-180) and (90,0)/(90,180) are the same physical point. All 40 must be kept (|lat| <= 90 and |lon| <= 180 are inclusive). Not a real track: a no-crash test for haversine/heading/mercator at the limits with exact coordinate repeats; detector counts are unconstrained.
